title: Universal factorization before Stein connectedness
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a universally closed and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and factor $f$ as $X\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{s}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization]. Then $q$ is universally closed, quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and surjective; $s$ is integral; $q_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$; and this factorization is the relative spectrum of $f_*\mathcal O_X$ and commutes with flat base change.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY, label lemma-stein-universally-closed, line 15087), clauses (1)--(5) and proof

proof.text: The universally closed, quasi-separated morphism $f$ is quasi-compact by the quasi-compactness permanence result [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Hence the normalization of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in $X$ is defined. The relative-normalization description [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] identifies the intermediate scheme locally with the spectrum of the integral closure of $A$ in $B=H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, while [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-global-sections-integral] says that this closure is all of $B$. Thus the intermediate scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the second map $s$ is integral, and the factorization is the relative spectrum of $f_*\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-pbc-stein-factorization].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY), proof using Morphisms Lemmas 03GI, 035H and 03GV

proof.text: The factor map $q$ is universally closed by the image-of-a-universally-closed-morphism lemma [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed], applied to the factorization after the image argument of the source. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since $s$ is affine and hence quasi-separated and $s\circ q=f$ is quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated by the same composition-permanence result because $s\circ q=f$ is quasi-separated. This gives all three morphism properties required for the subsequent pushforward argument.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY), proof using Morphisms Lemma 03GN and Schemes Lemmas 03GI, 01KV

proof.text: Since $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes $q_*\mathcal O_X$ quasi-coherent. On the affine target $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the global sections of this sheaf are $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=B$. The affine tilde/global-sections equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies a quasi-coherent sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the tilde of its global sections, so $q_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY), proof of clause (3), using Schemes Lemmas 01LC and 01IA

proof.text: The image of $q$ is closed because $q$ is universally closed. Write it as $V(I)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. For $h\in I$, the pullback of $h$ is a global section of $\mathcal O_X$ whose image in every residue field $\kappa(x)$ vanishes (for $x\in X$ the point $q(x)$ lies in $V(I)$, so $h\in I$ maps into $\mathfrak m_{q(x)}$ and the germ of $q^\sharp(h)$ at $x$ lies in $\mathfrak m_x$), hence is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent]. Since the pullback identifies $B$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $h$ itself is nilpotent. Thus $I$ is nil and $V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, proving that $q$ is surjective.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY), surjectivity paragraph

proof.text: For a flat base change of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, degree-zero flat base change for proper global sections is the same calculation supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-stein-flat-base-change-global-sections]. The relative-spectrum construction then commutes with this base change by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change], so the displayed Stein factorization commutes with every flat base change.

lean.statement: theorem stein_universally_closed_factor {A : CommRingCat.{u}} {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec A) [UniversallyClosed f] [QuasiSeparated f] : UniversallyClosed X.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiCompact X.toSpecΓ ∧ QuasiSeparated X.toSpecΓ ∧ Surjective X.toSpecΓ ∧ IsIntegralHom f.steinFactorizationBase ∧ IsIso X.toSpecΓ.c ∧ IsIso ((TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} f.steinFactorizationBase.base).map (⟨X.toSpecΓ.c⟩ : Scheme.sheaf (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} X.toSpecΓ.base).obj (Scheme.sheaf X))) ∧ (∀ (T B' X' : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Spec A) (_ : Flat g) (b : B' ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) (s' : B' ⟶ T) (x : X' ⟶ X) (q' : X' ⟶ B'), IsPullback b s' f.steinFactorizationBase g → IsPullback x q' X.toSpecΓ b → IsIso ((TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} s'.base).map (⟨q'.c⟩ : Scheme.sheaf B' ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} q'.base).obj (Scheme.sheaf X'))))
lean.note: Relative Spec is rendered by its canonical algebra identification along the integral (hence affine) second map; flat base change uses arbitrary Cartesian squares, not only affine bases.
